1. DEFECT: the fifth word written on the glove is misspelled. It reads AESTHTIC. Even spelled correctly at nine letters it would read AESTHETIC, and the brand is Venus Aesthetics, so that finger is wrong either way. It must never appear in the published cut.
2. THE FIX, single route, no options. Reframe the shot so the fifth finger sits outside the frame. AUDIO

GRADE AND FINISH

SLIDE 3, THE GAP BETWEEN STATIONS
1. Heading top left, black caps 60px: WHY 4 TO 6 WEEKS
2. Three numbered pointers under it, 34px black, each under 20 words:
3. 1. Laser only reaches hair that is in its growing phase.
4. 2. Not every hair grows at the same time, so one session cannot catch them all.
5. 3. The gap lets the next batch come through, and that is what the next station is for.

SLIDE 4, WHAT SKIPPING A STATION COSTS

2. A short gold line segment across the middle of the slide with station 3 drawn as a hollow dot instead of a solid one.

5. 2. Book the next station before you leave the current one.

1. Centre, black caps 68px, two lines: WHERE WOULD / YOUR LINE START?

1. Understand what this is before you cut it. The board is assembled in one sitting from prints of real course photos that already carry their own dates. It is a reconstruction of a real course, not a filmed fill, and nothing in the edit may suggest the camera sat on that wall for months.
2. Order the stages by the real dates printed on those photos, earliest first. Never reorder to look better.
3. Hard cuts only, no dissolves and no transitions. The camera never moves, so each cut simply moves you further along the board. No timelapse device, no ticking clock sound, no counter.
4. Text at 0:01, top centre, white semi bold 44pt, two lines: "One board." then "Weeks apart." Remove at 0:04.
5. Small month stamp bottom left as each stage appears, white 30pt, reading only the real month already printed on those photos, for example "September", then "October", then "November". Do not invent a month and do not add a day or a year.
6. No on screen claim about a number of weeks, a number of sessions, or how anyone's skin or body answered. No text anywhere saying twelve weeks.

8. At about 0:18 push in slowly on the full board, 5 percent zoom over 4 seconds, no faster.
9. Hold the last 2 seconds on the full board with no text at all.
10. End card, 2 seconds: white, charcoal centred "Venus Aesthetics", smaller line "Your course, your pace".
11. Consent and privacy: every photo used must already be covered by a signed media release in that client's file. Treatment areas only, no faces, no names, no file text visible. If a photo is not covered, it does not go on the board and it does not get filmed.
12. No retouching, no smoothing, no brightening of individual photos. If you would not hand the raw board to the client, reshoot the board instead.

PROP SHOOT. 20 minutes, phone only, no crew.

1. Who: one practitioner in uniform, hands only, no face needed. One more staff member to hold the phone and keep the board stages in order.
2. Where: the clinic corridor or a treatment room, plain wall, board hung at chest height. Choose a wall with no window glare behind it.
3. Kit: phone vertical, locked on a small tripod or propped on the trolley at board height, framed so the whole board plus a hand's width around it is in shot. Ring light at 45 degrees off camera left. No flash. Do not move the phone once it is set.
4. Props: one white foam board 40x50cm, 12 prints made from real treatment area photos in client files that carry a signed media release, each print already carrying its real month printed along the bottom edge before the shoot, one roll of cream washi tape, 12 brass push pins, one pair of gloves, a cloth to wipe the board. No marker on set.
5. Nobody writes a date on camera. The dates were set when those photos were taken and they are printed on the prints, so the hand only ever pins.
6. The beat, filmed in this order without moving the camera: (1) empty board, 4 seconds. (2) Gloved hand pins the earliest print, hold 4 seconds. (3) Rebuild the board to three prints, film 4 seconds, hand adjusts one pin. (4) Rebuild to seven prints, film 4 seconds, hand straightens one print. (5) Full board, hand steps back out of frame, film 6 seconds.
7. Direction: hands slow and deliberate. Nobody speaks, no music on set, let the pin click and the paper be heard. The camera staying put is the whole trick, so check the frame matches between every stage before rolling.
8. Time on set: 20 minutes, roughly 4 minutes per board stage.
9. Hard rule on set: no faces, no client names, nothing identifying anywhere in frame. If in doubt, leave that photo off the board.

production.conceptLine: A glass jar on the reception counter where a finished course of laser hair reduction ends with a razor going in, one physical object that turns a last session into content.
production.spec:
VIDEO EDIT, from the footage shot below
1. Cut to 18 to 22 seconds. Six shots. Nobody speaks in the whole reel.
2. Shot order in the timeline: wide of the counter, close on the jar with the lid off, the hand holding the razor above the opening, the drop, the razor settling, the lid going back on. That is the caption's lid off, clink, lid on, in that order, so do not reorder it.
3. Text at 0:00, top centre, white, bold, 2 lines: "Last session." then "Razor goes in the jar."
4. Keep the real clink at full volume. Duck the music to silence for the half second around it, then bring it back.

6. Text at about 0:09, bottom third, white, 1 line: "One jar. One course at a time."
7. At about 0:15, bottom third: "The jar lives at reception."
8. Last 2 seconds: the closed jar in frame, no text, no music tail.
9. Venus wordmark, small, bottom left, last 1.5 seconds only.

DESIGNER NOTES
11. Never write permanent, painless or forever on screen. The jar is the idea, not a promise.
12. No count anywhere, on screen or in the framing. Nothing that says or implies how many people have finished a course.
13. No price, no offer, no percentage.

production.recordGuide:
1. Who: one front desk staff member in uniform, confident, plus one pair of hands for the drop. Nobody speaks on camera.
2. Where: the reception counter, with the Venus wordmark or plain marble behind. Clear the counter of papers, phones, cups and files first.
3. Kit: phone, vertical, on a small tripod or propped on books at counter height. Natural light from the entrance, plus the ring light at 50 percent from the left.
4. Props: one large clear glass jar with a lid, 10 to 12 inches tall. Six to ten brand new disposable razors, taken out of their packets on set. One small printed card, white, 3 by 2 inches, black type reading THE LAST RAZOR, leaning inside the jar or propped in front of it. One clean cloth to wipe fingerprints off the glass before every shot.
5. Dressing the jar: two or three razors resting in the base, no more. A jar filled to the middle reads as a tally of finished clients, and we are not claiming a tally.
6. Hygiene, not optional: only new, unopened razors go in the jar. Never collect a used blade from a client, and keep the lid on between takes.
7. The beat: 1) wide of the counter with the jar in frame, 2) step in close on the jar with the lid off, 3) a hand enters frame and holds the razor above the opening for one beat, 4) the drop, with the room silent so the clink records clean, 5) close on the razor settling in the base, 6) the staff member puts the lid back on and smiles at the jar, not at the lens.
8. Direction: slow hands, no rush, no laughing, no talking. Shoot the drop 4 times so the edit has one clean clink. Ask everyone in reception to stay quiet for those four takes.

VIDEO EDIT, from the footage shot below

2. Score graphic: bottom right, a black rounded box at 70 percent opacity, white bold number inside, format 6/10, number large enough to read on a phone at arm's length.
3. Verdict line: directly above the score box, white bold, 1 line only, exactly as written below.
4. Prop 1, threading. Score 6/10. Verdict: "Accurate. Also your eyes water."
5. Prop 2, wax strips. Score 5/10. Verdict: "Works. Sounds like Velcro."
6. Prop 3, epilator. Score 2/10. Verdict: "A machine that holds a grudge."
7. Prop 4, cream. Score 3/10. Verdict: "Open a window first."
8. Prop 5, razor. Score 7/10. Verdict: "Reliable. Every second day. Forever."
9. The caption's three beat line quotes the six and the two, so the threading score and the epilator score must stay exactly as written above.
10. Each score lands with a hard cut, not a fade. Put the cut on the beat of the audio.
11. Closing card, 3 seconds, black background, white text, 2 lines: "We are not scoring ours." then "Come and judge it yourself."
12. Audio: one trending audio with a clear beat, 60 percent volume, staff voices on top at full.
13. Burn captions for every verdict so it works on mute.
14. Export 1080 x 1920. Also export the epilator section alone as a 10 second Stories cut.

15. Do not score any Venus treatment out of ten. We are not the joke and we are not the winner.
16. Tape over or blur every brand label on every prop. We never name another brand.
17. No price, no offer, no percentage.
18. On screen text always says hair reduction, never hair removal. The phrase hair removal is never burned into a frame, not even on a prop label.

1. Who: two staff members in uniform, the two with the most personality. One holds the prop, the other gives the verdict, then they swap for the next prop.

6. The beat: they hold the prop up to the lens, react, deliver the one line verdict, put it down, next prop. Order is threading, wax strips, epilator, cream, razor.
7. Direction: deadpan, not shouty. Straight down the lens. Let them disagree with each other on exactly one prop, because that is the moment people reply to. English only, no Urdu words at all.

6. Runtime maths: 1 second opening card, 35 seconds of statements, 2 second end frame, 38 seconds total.
7. Buzzer on every myth cut, bell on the truth cut. Loud, but not clipping.
8. Burn English subtitles the whole way through: white semibold 34pt, bottom third, maximum two lines, never covering a face.
9. Cut on the laugh, not after it. Dead air kills this format.
10. Music: upbeat at 20 percent under the voices, cut it dead on the final verdict stamp.
11. Do not add a single Roman Urdu word on screen, even as a joke.
12. Nothing on screen about results, session counts, or how anyone felt during a treatment. This is a myths format, not a results format.
13. No staff names and no client names on screen.
14. End frame, 2 seconds: both staff looking at the lens, text white semibold 40pt: ASK US THE ONES YOU ARE NOT SURE ABOUT

production.recordGuide:
SHOOT, 20 minutes including printing, phone only, no crew
1. Who: two staff in black uniform. Pick the two who are naturally funniest on camera. One is the quizmaster with the buzzer, one answers. Swap roles halfway.

Winter is easier because there is less sun on the skin. 3) Myth. It targets a pocket of fat, it is not weight loss. 4) Truth. Shave the area before you come, unless we have told you otherwise. 5) Myth. The patch test is read 48 hours later and it sets your settings.

1. Who: one person part way through or at the end of a laser course. A staff member is the easiest and safest option. If it is a client, take a signed consent slip first and keep it on file, and show only her forearm or lower leg, never her face. She is never named, in the caption or on screen.

1. Structure: 3 second setup, then four rounds of about 6 seconds, then a 3 second sign off. That is 30 seconds, inside the range.
2. 0:00 to 0:03. Open on her tying the blindfold, mid shot, her laughing. No logo and no intro card.
3. Text at 0:00, top of the safe area, white Instrument Sans Bold 62 px on a 70 percent black pill: "Name the machine. Sound only."

   a. Round card for 12 frames: porcelain #F7F3EE full frame, centred Fraunces Bold 80 px ink, "ROUND 1" to "ROUND 4".
   b. 2 seconds of the machine running with the camera on the handpiece, not on her. Device sound at full level.

11. Only the four approved machines appear or are named in this reel: laser, RF skin tightening, RF microneedling, fat freezing applicator. If any other device is visible in the background, crop it out or reframe. No other treatment word goes on screen.
12. No claim about comfort, results, session counts or prices anywhere on screen.
13. Cover frame for the grid: her blindfolded, mid laugh, with the step 3 line on it.
14. Stories cut, 12 seconds: round 1 in full and round 4 in full, cut exactly as step 4 builds them, nothing else. Add an Instagram quiz sticker over round 1 when it goes up.

production.recordGuide:
1. Who: one staff member in uniform who is happy to look silly, plus one colleague off camera to run the machines and one to hold the phone. Three people total. No names on screen and no names in the caption.
2. Where: one treatment room with the machines wheeled in together. Plain wall behind her, no posters and no other branding in shot.

production.title: Real Talk

production.title: The Results
production.hook: Same brush. Same twenty strokes. We start counting today.
production.conceptLine: A hairbrush becomes the measuring instrument for a PRP course, filmed today as the honest baseline with the second brush sealed and banked for the follow up.
production.spec:
WHAT THIS POST IS AND IS NOT
1. This post publishes the BASELINE brush only. Today we film brush one, the count and the date. We do not show a second brush and we do not imply a result.
2. The comparison post goes out only when a real, consenting patient reaches that point in their course and the second brush physically exists. There is no publishing schedule for it and the caption must never promise one. Never stage the second brush. Never add or remove hair from a brush. Never film two brushes on the same day and present them as different dates.
3. Nothing in this post states how much hair fell, how it compares to anything, or how the patient feels about it. The frame is the evidence, the caption does not narrate it.

FINAL LENGTH: 22 seconds. 3 plus 8 plus 4 plus 4 plus 3 equals 22. Check the total on the timeline.

THE CUT
1. 0:00 to 0:03. Close on the clean empty brush lying on the black card. No text yet, no logo, no intro card.
2. 0:03 to 0:11. The brushing, with the count. Keep the real audio of the counting. Let it run, do not cut inside the count.
3. 0:11 to 0:15. The brush is laid back on the taped position. Cut to the top down macro of the bristles and hold dead still for a full 3 seconds so people can actually look.
4. 0:15 to 0:19. The date being written on the white card and placed beside the brush.
5. 0:19 to 0:22. Hold on brush plus date together. This is the frame the follow up post has to match exactly.

BURNED IN TEXT. White, bold, top third, one line at a time.
6. 0:03: Twenty strokes. Same brush. Same light.
7. 0:11: This is day one of a PRP course
8. 0:15: We will film the same brush again
9. 0:19 to end: no text.
10. Nothing on screen says when the next film happens. No month, no week count, no date beyond the one written on the card.

AUDIO
11. Room tone and the counting only. No music. No trending audio on a tracking post.

CONTINUITY TO BANK NOW FOR THE FOLLOW UP FILM
12. Note and save all of these: phone position, height, lens, exposure lock value, white balance value, the exact light setup, the brush model, the stroke count, the time of day.
13. Write those nine values into the calendar sheet for the follow up shoot. If any one of them changes, the comparison is worthless.
14. One grade, no filter, no skin smoothing, no sharpening on the macro.

EXPORTS
15. Feed reel 1080x1920.
16. Stories cut, 8 seconds: the count and the macro hold only.
17. Export the macro frame at native resolution and archive it in the patient folder with the date in the file name.

QA BEFORE HANDOVER
18. No invented quote, no invented review, no named result, no personal name in the caption or on screen.
19. No before and after wording anywhere on this post.
20. Signed consent on file before this is scheduled.
21. No facial treatment is named anywhere. English only on screen.
production.recordGuide:
1. Who: one real patient who is starting a PRP course at Venus this week, plus one staff member to hold the phone. Written consent signed before anything is filmed. The face is not needed, so offer a hands and hair only version to make the yes easy.
2. Where: one treatment room, plain wall, a plain table pulled to the window. Shoot the same room every time this series returns.
3. Kit: phone on a small tripod or propped on books at chest height, vertical. One ring light at 45 degrees from the left, or a north facing window with the blind fully up. Lock exposure and white balance before take one and write both values down.
4. Props: one new wide tooth brush in a pale colour so dark hair reads against it. One identical second brush, sealed in a bag, dated with a marker, stored in the same room for the follow up. One matte black A3 card as the surface. One plain white A5 card for the date. A black marker. Masking tape to mark the exact brush position and the exact phone position.
5. The beat: lay the tape marks. Clean brush down, film 3 seconds. Patient brushes crown to ends while the staff member counts out loud to twenty. Brush back on the taped mark. Macro top down on the bristles, held still. Date written on the white card and placed beside the brush. Final hold on both.
6. Direction: nobody talks about results, nobody promises anything, nobody says the word permanent, and nobody says when the next film will be. The only speech in the whole shoot is the count, in English. Keep the counting calm, not dramatic. Two takes maximum so a third brushing does not disturb the hair.
7. Time on set: 18 minutes including laying the tape marks.
production.refWhy: Sono Bello's progress over time reel at 2.16 percent is the same promise, a measurement started in public and returned to later, filmed without any claim attached.

production.title: Real Talk
production.hook: Two staff, one concern, zero agreement.
production.conceptLine: Two Venus staff publicly disagree about where to start on the same concern, one block each straight to camera, and the comments decide it.
production.spec:
THE DEBATE. One concern, two treatments, both from the Venus menu. Concern: cheeks and a jawline that look tired and uneven. Side A argues RF microneedling, start with the texture. Side B argues RF skin tightening, start with the firmness. Neither side is arguing for a facial, and no facial treatment is named by anyone at any point.

FINAL LENGTH: 38 seconds. 3 plus 13 plus 13 plus 5 plus 4 equals 38. Check the total on the timeline.

THE CUT
1. 0:00 to 0:03. Title card laid over the room, not over black. Black bar across the lower third, white caps: SAME CONCERN. TWO TREATMENTS. Second line smaller: cheeks and a jawline that look tired and uneven
2. 0:03 to 0:16. Side A to camera, full frame, no split screen. Bottom left, a persistent gold tag: TEAM MICRONEEDLING
3. 0:16 to 0:29. Side B to camera. Same framing, same distance, same height. Bottom left tag: TEAM SKIN TIGHTENING
4. 0:29 to 0:34. The best interruption from the takes, where they talk over each other. Keep it messy, keep the laugh.
5. 0:34 to 0:38. Both in frame, shrug to camera, then the closing line lands.

ON SCREEN TEXT
6. The two tags stay up for the whole of each side's block and never appear together.
7. At 0:08 and again at 0:21, one short pull quote from what they actually said, white bold, top third, six words maximum. Take the words off the take, do not write them in advance.
8. Closing line at 0:34, centred: Neither of them decides. Your skin does.
9. Second closing line at 0:36, smaller: Bring the concern to an assessment.
10. No score counter, no versus graphic with numbers, no poll graphic in the feed cut.

AUDIO
11. Real voices at full. One light instrumental bed at 12 percent under the talking, cut it completely at 0:29 so the interruption is heard clean.
12. No trending audio that would bury the arguments.

SUBTITLES
13. Burn in English subtitles for every spoken word. Two lines maximum on screen, sat above the tags, never overlapping them.
14. If anyone slips into Urdu on a take, that take is unusable. Reshoot it, do not subtitle over it.
15. If either of them names a facial treatment on a take, that take is unusable too. Reshoot rather than cut around it, because the subtitles would carry the word.

EXPORTS
16. Feed reel 1080x1920.
17. Stories cut, 15 seconds: title card, the strongest six seconds from each side, the shrug. Add a two option poll sticker to the Stories version only, options TEAM MICRONEEDLING and TEAM SKIN TIGHTENING.
18. Cover frame: both staff in frame mid disagreement.

QA BEFORE HANDOVER
19. Neither side claims a result, a cure, a session count, a recovery date, or that one treatment is better for everyone.
20. Nobody describes what a client felt or how long anything lasted.
21. The words permanent, painless, guaranteed and flawless appear nowhere, spoken or written.
22. No comment YES, no tag a friend, no double tap, anywhere.
23. No prices, no offers, no percentages.
24. The debate stays inside the approved menu: laser hair reduction, skin tightening, fat freezing, PRP for hair, Venus Viva resurfacing, dermapen. Nothing from outside it is named on a card, in the subtitles, in the tags or in the caption.
25. No personal name on screen or in the caption. Staff are staff.
production.recordGuide:
1. Who: two staff members who can hold an opinion on camera, in clean uniform. Pick the two who already argue about this in the staff room. Brief them 10 minutes before on the rebuilt debate, microneedling first versus tightening first, and do not hand them a script to memorise.
2. Where: one treatment room, plain wall behind, no clutter and no product shelf in shot. Both sides shot against the identical wall so the swap between them is invisible.
3. Kit: phone on a tripod, vertical, chest height, framed waist up with headroom for the top third text. One ring light straight on. Exposure and white balance locked before take one and not touched again.
4. Props: two A4 cards printed TEAM MICRONEEDLING and TEAM SKIN TIGHTENING, held only in the shrug shot at the end. One phone stopwatch running off camera to cap each side at 30 seconds on set, which the edit cuts to 13. Two identical chairs, or both standing, not one of each.
5. The beat: read the concern out loud once off camera, cheeks and a jawline that look tired and uneven. Side A talks to camera for up to 30 seconds. Side B talks to camera for up to 30 seconds. Then both in frame, one line each at the same time, then the shrug.
6. Direction: talk to the lens and not to each other during the two arguments. Leave in the moment at the end where they do talk over each other, that beat is the whole post. Keep it to plain words about what each treatment is for. Nobody names a treatment outside the Venus menu, nobody says a treatment is better for everyone, nobody promises a result or a timeline, nobody mentions a price. English only, no Roman Urdu. Three takes maximum, the first take is usually the honest one.
7. Time on set: 22 minutes including the briefing.
production.refWhy: Pulse Light let staff personality carry the film rather than a script, which is exactly what a two sided argument needs, and the original trending audio reference contradicted this post's own no trending audio rule.

production.title: Real Talk
production.hook: Six weeks to the first wedding.
production.conceptLine: The wedding season group chat at six weeks out, acted by the team, ending on the only advice that actually helps, start early and start with one thing.
production.spec:
EDIT STEPS for the footage you shoot

1. Build the chat mock before anything else. On a phone, create a group called "Wedding Countdown" with three contacts named Bride, Cousin and Me. Type the messages in English only. Screen record 8 seconds of the messages arriving with the typing dots between them.
2. Message order in the mock: "Six weeks to the first wedding", typing dots, "I have a list", typing dots, "Where do I even start".
3. Cut the reel to 24 seconds.
4. 0:00 to 0:03: the screen recording full frame. No added text. The message is the hook.
5. At 0:03, cut to the phone in a hand in the room, then widen to the three staff members.
6. 0:03 to 0:08: the panicker reads her list out loud, fast, in one breath. The list is exactly six items and every one is drawn from this set only: laser hair reduction, skin tightening, fat freezing, PRP for hair, Venus Viva resurfacing, dermapen. No facial, no peel, no drug brand name, no device brand other than Venus Viva.
7. 0:08 to 0:12: the calm one answers with one line only, "One thing at a time." Hold on her face for a beat after she stops.
8. 0:12 to 0:16: the third staff member looks up from her phone and asks what happened, because she has not read the chat. One beat of silence, then a hard cut.
9. 0:16 to 0:21: all three look at the lens. Text centre, Instrument Sans semibold 48 white in a 35% black pill: "Start early. Start with one thing."
10. 0:21 to 0:24 end card: porcelain #F6F1EA, 2px bronze #A97C4F rule, ink Fraunces 40 "Venus Aesthetics", under it Instrument Sans 24 "Call or WhatsApp".
11. Trending audio under the room sound at 15%, ducked to 5% whenever anyone speaks. Do not pick a track with lyrics over the dialogue.
12. Subtitle every spoken line, Instrument Sans semibold 40 white, bottom third, English only, two lines maximum.
13. Nothing on screen names a price, a percentage or an injectable brand. The printed list the panicker holds must not be readable in frame.
14. Nobody states a result, a number of sessions or how long anything lasted. The joke is the chat, not an outcome.
15. Export a 10 second Stories cut: the chat mock plus the final line.
production.recordGuide:
1. Who: three staff members in uniform, no doctor. One is calm, one is the panicker, one has not read the chat.
2. Where: the staff room or an empty consultation room. Plain wall, no branding in shot except the logo on the uniform.
3. Kit: one phone, vertical, chest height, propped on a stack of files. Window light or a ring light to the side. A second phone to screen record the chat mock.
4. Props: three phones, one gold wedding invitation card, one printed A5 list of six treatments held face down, a chair, a cup of tea. Every prop word is English.
5. The beat: invitation lands on the desk, phone one lights up, the panicker reads her list, the calm one says one line, the third looks up and asks what happened, all three turn to the lens.
6. Direction: deadpan throughout, no shouting, nobody looks at the camera until the last beat. English only. Two takes of each beat, the second one faster.
7. Time on set: 20 minutes including the chat mock screen recording.
production.refWhy: A reel carried by a trending audio and a played out scene rather than a treatment, which is the format this group chat needs.

production.title: The Results
production.hook: One board. Weeks apart. No retouching.
production.conceptLine: A board on the clinic wall where prints from real courses are pinned up under the dates they already carry, filmed from one fixed camera position so each stage of the board is another point in a real course rather than a staged countdown.
production.spec:
VIDEO EDIT of the filmed material. Reel, 1080x1920, finished length 22 to 28 seconds.

1. Understand what this is before you cut it. The board is assembled in one sitting from prints of real course photos that already carry their own dates. It is a reconstruction of a real course, not a filmed fill, and nothing in the edit may suggest the camera sat on that wall for months.
2. Order the stages by the real dates printed on those photos, earliest first. Never reorder to look better.
3. Hard cuts only, no dissolves and no transitions. The camera never moves, so each cut simply moves you further along the board. No timelapse device, no ticking clock sound, no counter.
4. Text at 0:01, top centre, white semi bold 44pt, two lines: "One board." then "Weeks apart." Remove at 0:04.
5. Small month stamp bottom left as each stage appears, white 30pt, reading only the real month already printed on those photos, for example "September", then "October", then "November". Do not invent a month and do not add a day or a year.
6. No on screen claim about a number of weeks, a number of sessions, or how anyone's skin or body answered. No text anywhere saying twelve weeks.
7. Keep the on set sound: the pin going in, paper, the room. Music from 0:06 at 15 percent, soft and low.
8. At about 0:18 push in slowly on the full board, 5 percent zoom over 4 seconds, no faster.
9. Hold the last 2 seconds on the full board with no text at all.
10. End card, 2 seconds: white, charcoal centred "Venus Aesthetics", smaller line "Your course, your pace".
11. Consent and privacy: every photo used must already be covered by a signed media release in that client's file. Treatment areas only, no faces, no names, no file text visible. If a photo is not covered, it does not go on the board and it does not get filmed.
12. No retouching, no smoothing, no brightening of individual photos. If you would not hand the raw board to the client, reshoot the board instead.
13. Grid cover frame: the full board, straight on.
14. Also export a 10 second Stories cut: empty board, three photos, full board.
production.recordGuide:
PROP SHOOT. 20 minutes, phone only, no crew.

1. Who: one practitioner in uniform, hands only, no face needed. One more staff member to hold the phone and keep the board stages in order.
2. Where: the clinic corridor or a treatment room, plain wall, board hung at chest height. Choose a wall with no window glare behind it.
3. Kit: phone vertical, locked on a small tripod or propped on the trolley at board height, framed so the whole board plus a hand's width around it is in shot. Ring light at 45 degrees off camera left. No flash. Do not move the phone once it is set.
4. Props: one white foam board 40x50cm, 12 prints made from real treatment area photos in client files that carry a signed media release, each print already carrying its real month printed along the bottom edge before the shoot, one roll of cream washi tape, 12 brass push pins, one pair of gloves, a cloth to wipe the board. No marker on set.
5. Nobody writes a date on camera. The dates were set when those photos were taken and they are printed on the prints, so the hand only ever pins.
6. The beat, filmed in this order without moving the camera: (1) empty board, 4 seconds. (2) Gloved hand pins the earliest print, hold 4 seconds. (3) Rebuild the board to three prints, film 4 seconds, hand adjusts one pin. (4) Rebuild to seven prints, film 4 seconds, hand straightens one print. (5) Full board, hand steps back out of frame, film 6 seconds.
7. Direction: hands slow and deliberate. Nobody speaks, no music on set, let the pin click and the paper be heard. The camera staying put is the whole trick, so check the frame matches between every stage before rolling.
8. Time on set: 20 minutes, roughly 4 minutes per board stage.
9. Hard rule on set: no faces, no client names, nothing identifying anywhere in frame. If in doubt, leave that photo off the board.
production.refWhy: Sono Bello's progress over time reel at 2.16 percent shows how to carry a course visually without narrating a result, which is the exact line this post had crossed.

production.title: Real Talk
production.variant: Explain your job to a five year old
production.hook: Explain your job. No big words.
production.conceptLine: Staff have to explain their own job with every technical word banned, and a bell rings the moment one slips out, so the clinic explains itself in language anyone can follow.
production.spec:
VIDEO EDIT of the filmed material. Reel, 1080x1920, finished length 30 to 35 seconds.

1. Open on the first fumble, mid sentence. No intro card, no logo, no setup shot.
2. Text at 0:00, top centre, white bold 46pt, two lines: "Explain your job" then "No big words". Remove at 0:03.
3. Under it from 0:03 to 0:07, smaller white 30pt, two lines: "Banned: laser, radiofrequency, collagen," then "platelets, microneedling, fat freezing". Six words on the cards, six words banned on screen, matching the caption. Remove at 0:07.
4. Role chip bottom left as each person starts, charcoal chip, white 32pt, role only and never a name, for example "Front desk", "Therapist", "Practitioner". Hold 3 seconds each.
5. Keep every bell ring in. On each bell, add a 4 frame zoom punch of 6 percent and a single frame white flash. The bell is the concept, so at least one ring must survive the cut.
6. Three answers, one per person, matching the three staff in the record guide. Cut each one the moment the point lands, do not let an answer run past 8 seconds.
7. Put the best answer last and hold 2 seconds of silence on that person's face after they finish.
8. Subtitles for every spoken word, white 38pt, maximum 5 words per line, 220px above the bottom edge. No names in the subtitles, cut around any moment where someone says a colleague's name.
9. Music: none for the first 7 seconds so the fumbling carries. Light playful bed from 0:07 at 20 percent.
10. Nothing stays in that promises a result, a timeline or a number of sessions. If someone drifts into what a treatment will do for you, cut it.
11. End card, 2 seconds: black, white centred "Venus Aesthetics", smaller line "We will explain it properly in person too".
12. Leave the stumbles, the laughing and the restarts in. Polish kills this one.
13. Grid cover frame: a staff member mid gesture, mouth open, not a posed smile.
14. Also export a 12 second Stories cut of the single best answer.
production.recordGuide:
ENGAGEMENT SHOOT. 20 minutes, phone only, no crew.

1. Who: three staff in uniform, one practitioner, one from the front desk, one therapist. Pick the three who talk most easily, not the three most senior.
2. Where: treatment room with a plain wall behind, or the reception counter with the clinic wall behind. One location only, everyone in the same spot.
3. Kit: phone vertical, chest height, propped on a tripod or a stack of files, subject 1.5 metres away so the phone microphone picks the voice up cleanly. Ring light straight on. Natural room light is fine if the window is behind the camera.
4. Props: six A5 cards printed with one word each in large black type: LASER, RADIOFREQUENCY, COLLAGEN, PLATELETS, MICRONEEDLING, FAT FREEZING. One desk bell or a phone buzzer sound. One chair.
5. The beat: each person draws a card, reads it silently, then explains that thing straight to camera using no technical words, including the word printed on their own card. Whoever holds the bell rings it the second a banned word slips out, and that person starts again from the beginning. Three people, three cards drawn, the other three cards stay in the pile.
6. Direction: one take per person, no rehearsing and no scripting. Push them towards everyday comparisons from their own life, kitchen, ironing, gardening, whatever they reach for. English only throughout, and English prop words only. If a line lands, do not ask for a cleaner version of it.
7. Nobody promises anything on camera. Explaining what a machine does is the game, telling a viewer what it will do for them is not.
8. Time on set: 20 minutes, about 6 minutes per person including the restarts.
9. Do not let anyone read from a phone or a note. The struggle is the content.
production.refWhy: Sculpt Spa's deadpan reel at 4.46 percent proves staff struggling straight to camera outperforms polish, which is what the bell and the restarts are here to protect.
production.refMetric: 2k plays, 95 likes, 4.46% ER, the best humour result in the audit

production.title: The Team
production.conceptLine: The two hours nobody sees, filmed in real order at nine in the morning, from the key in the door to the kettle, ending when the doors actually open at eleven.
production.spec:
VIDEO EDIT of the filmed material. Reel, 1080x1920, finished length 25 to 30 seconds.

1. Keep the shots in the real order they were filmed. Do not reorder for pace, the chronology is the concept and the caption says so out loud.
2. Text at 0:00, top centre, white semi bold 44pt, two lines: "9:00 AM" then "Before anyone arrives". Remove at 0:03.
3. Real time stamps top right, small white 28pt, appearing on each new shot and matching the actual clock on set, for example 9:02, 9:09, 9:18, 9:35, 10:10. If a stamp does not match the clock in that shot, fix the stamp, never the shot.
4. The five things the caption names must all be in the cut and in this order: lights on, blinds up, tray laid out, machine warming, kettle. Nothing in the caption that is not on screen.
5. Final shot carries the stamp "11:00" with a second line under it, white 32pt: "Doors open".
6. Keep the natural sound for the first 10 seconds: the key, the light switch, the couch roll tearing, the kettle click. No music at all until 0:10.
7. Soft piano or ambient bed from 0:10 at 18 percent. Never loud enough to bury the kettle.
8. Cut on action, not on the beat. Let two or three shots run a full 4 seconds so it breathes.
9. No speed ramps, no timelapse and no captions over the middle section. Silence is doing the work here.
10. Last 2 seconds: hold on the unlocked front door from inside, no text.
11. End card, 2 seconds: white, charcoal centred "Venus Aesthetics", smaller line "Open at eleven".
12. Privacy: no client names, no appointment screens legible, no faces except staff. Blur any name on the tablet or diary, and no staff name on screen either.
13. Grid cover frame: the moment the treatment room lights come on.
14. Also export a 10 second Stories cut: lights on, tray set, kettle, doors open.
production.recordGuide:
ENGAGEMENT SHOOT. 20 minutes, filmed during a real 9am open. Phone only, no crew.

1. Who: the two staff who actually open the branch, in uniform. One films, one works. Nobody speaks to camera and there is no presenter.
2. Where: one branch, moving inward in the order it happens: front door, reception, corridor, treatment room, staff kitchen.
3. Kit: phone vertical, handheld, no ring light and no extra lamps. Use only the light that is there, including the dark moment before the switch goes on. Wipe the lens first.
4. Props, all real and already in the clinic: door keys, the light switch panel, blinds, couch roll, clean metal tray, sterile pouches, gloves, the machine power button, the kettle, two cups, the appointment tablet or diary, a cloth.
5. The beat, filmed in this exact order: (1) key into the front door. (2) Hand hits the light switch and the room lifts from dark to lit, hold through the change. (3) Blinds open. (4) Couch roll pulled and torn. (5) Tray set, sterile pouches laid in a row. (6) Machine switched on, hold on its ready light. (7) Kettle filled and clicked. (8) First appointment checked on the tablet, screen angled away so nothing is readable. (9) Both staff sit for 10 seconds with tea, saying nothing. (10) Front door unlocked.
6. Note the real clock time as each shot is filmed and send that list to the editor, the on screen stamps come from it.
7. Direction: one slow continuous pass if the phone can hold it steady, otherwise ten separate shots of 3 to 4 seconds each. No talking, no posing, nobody looks at the lens until the final shot.
8. Time on set: 20 minutes inside the real opening routine. Do not stage this at two in the afternoon, the light gives it away instantly.
9. Privacy on set: no client names spoken or filmed, no screens with data, no faces other than staff.
